analysis: The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. The visible changed ranges are the date stamp (line 3) and operator-filter documentation for load_model (head 1412-1414), prefetch_model (1422-1424) and desired_models (1456-1464). No executable code, keys, authorization logic or wire behavior is modified. The documentation describes the provider refusing a coordinator-directed load, prefetch or desired-model convergence for a model outside the operator's enabled model filter, with `model_not_selected`. The desired_models text also says an alias successor outside the filter is not fetched, staged or served, and the previous build is not dropped. This tightens provider-side control against a coordinator-directed model change. The coordinator is trusted, but the provider still enforces local operator policy. It does not weaken any threat-model assumption in A-004, T-012 or T-027. The text also says that with Autopilot enabled, only its lease and set gates can admit such a build. That is consistent with the surrounding Autopilot text (model_autopilot_control, selected_models, shadow lease). The rest of the supplied excerpt is unchanged context: cache receipt v2, GLM and MiMo prompt contract, capacity probe and Autopilot state. It was not examined as a change and raises no new issue. A statement in the unchanged text (around line 1003) that off-catalog local models are owner-only routable matches existing T-041/T-053-style scoping. Remaining integration question, not a finding: the implementation claims (`autopilotAllowsModel`, `operatorFilterAllows` in ProviderLoop+ModelSelection.swift) were not supplied, so whether the code matches this doc cannot be verified here. This is a documentation-accuracy matter only, and no security regression is evidenced.
